function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning:
The user says "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, you need to start the Docker Desktop or Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use `net start com.docker.service` or `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` in PowerShell. Or if using Docker Desktop, you can launch the application.

But the user might want to start Docker engine via command line. We can use `docker-machine start default` if using Docker Machine. But nowadays Docker Desktop uses a service named `com.docker.service`. So we can run `net start com.docker.service`.

We have a tool to execute commands on Windows. We can call the function with command: `net start com.docker.service`. That will start the Docker service. Alternatively, we can use PowerShell: `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. But the tool expects a string of Windows command line instructions. So we can pass `net start com.docker.service`.

Thus we should call the function.
